works.abstract_text: Extending Zhu's Pell-prime result (2011), we refute the conjecture in OEIS A320043, COMMENTS, revision 43 (September 8, 2022; posed December 16, 2018), by a(708158976)=144767444036350576^2. For every prime p, its preceding row has sum p^2(p^2-1)/12; for p>=5, this sum is a square exactly when p^2-12y^2=1 for an integer y. An elementary descent recovers the known Pell sequence and proves that this is the smallest additional square index whose successor is prime. We also reprove the known power-of-two index restriction, give a factor excluding the proposed next candidate in A277434, and prove the triangle's product identity and an all-row divisor formula.

works.abstract_text: We answer Section 4, item 3 of Alikhani and Griswold's On the Integer Domination Root Conjecture by constructing connected graphs with domination root −4 and unbounded order. Joining r copies of their 33-vertex graph through vertices adjacent to leaves gives a connected graph on 33r vertices whose domination polynomial is the rth power of the original polynomial. The root −4 has multiplicity exactly r, and the copies can be joined along a path with maximum degree seven. A mixed construction gives examples of every order at least 35, with maximum degree seven and cycle rank four. We give a complete set-bijection proof, an exact finite calculation for the base graph, and the scope of the corresponding Lean declarations.

works.abstract_text: We prove Anthony Browne's conjecture in OEIS A164660, final FORMULA (29 May 2016): for every positive integer n, the reduced numerator of the integral from 0 to 1 of T_(n+1)(x) equals the stated floor product and (-1)^(n/rad(n)). Both sides are +1 exactly when 4 divides n. The same calculation proves the preceding rational-integral conjecture and gives its denominator sequence A164661. More generally, replacing the exponent n in the product by any integer r >= 2, and translating its interval by any integer, leaves the product unchanged. We give the exact root count for every r >= 1 and correct two coefficient-table discrepancies in the linked sources.

works.abstract_text: Bajnok–Beatty Conjecture 4.1 in arXiv:2406.04045v1, Section 4, p. 10, asks which groups Z/2Z × Z/(2k)Z have a two-element signed spanning set of radius s. The note proves its four-case classification for all positive k,s. A near-square relation-lattice argument gives the necessary congruences, and explicit constructions give sufficiency. Coefficient-residue counts also prove Conjecture 1.6 (Section 1, p. 3): for s≥3, the maximum noncyclic order is 2s² if 2s+1 is prime, and 2s²+2s−(p²−1)/2 otherwise, where p is the smallest prime divisor of 2s+1. The attaining constructions are those of Bajnok and Beatty. The bounds in Theorems 1.8, 3.2 and 3.3 hold without regularity. For Conjecture 1.10 the note proves cyclicity for two generators and corrects the printed multiplier domain by an explicit perfect set in Z/13Z.

We reprove Bala's two divisibilities (Bala, 2026) and deduce product divisibility by (6n+1)(10n+1), preservation of the parity criterion, and counting and ordered recursions. We give written alternative proofs of the eleven XOR identities in A048718, verified by Karlsson (2022) with Walnut. works.abstract_text: We refute the mixed-state inverse sumset estimate expected in Remark 45, equation (58), of Bu, Gu and Jaffe, Quantum Ruzsa Divergence to Quantify Magic (arXiv:2401.14385v3). A computationally diagonal equal mixture of two basis states in dimension seven has quantum-doubling constant sqrt(2) and relative entropy log(7/2) from its mean state, while the proposed bound is at most (1/2)log(7). The contradiction uses exact inequalities and persists for every tensor power. For the same family, we verify that the weaker estimate (59) has a positive denominator and holds strictly, and give the equality case of the companion entropy-growth statement for computationally diagonal states.

works.abstract_text: We prove the conjecture in §2.9 of Lester, Haddadin and Gripaios, Lorentz and permutation invariants of particles III (arXiv:2008.05206v6), that their three-variable sets S and S-hat are minimal for their respective four-particle event classes. Any two continuous, Lorentz- and pair-permutation-invariant, parity-odd real variables vanish together on a chiral collision event. The proof constructs a sphere consisting entirely of chiral events, on which parity acts antipodally up to the allowed symmetries, and applies the two-dimensional Borsuk-Ulam theorem. The same obstruction holds for strictly timelike, momentum-completable collisions with any number of additional interchangeable momenta, and for fully interchangeable collections of at least four momenta.

works.abstract_text: We refute the trace-distance case of axiom (T4) of Denis, Lacaille, Martin and Serrano-Ensástiga (arXiv:2605.29436v1, Section III.A.2, Eq. (22) with p=1; (T4) in Section II.B, Eqs. (7)–(8)), where “a proof is left open.” An explicit SU(2)-covariant channel decreases the order-seven anticoherence of a mixed spin-four state by exactly 95/90552, disproving the universal validity suggested by their reported numerical evidence. The channel is a normalized sum of quadrupole Kraus operations; its covariance and trace preservation follow from Cartesian tensor identities. Both reduced states are diagonal, so the strict inequality reduces to rational arithmetic. We reconstruct an existing spin-four witness and give a self-contained exact counterexample within the full mixed-state domain of the proposed axiom.

works.abstract_text: Conjectures 3 and 4 in Section 5.2 of Huang, Stoica, Xia and Zhong, arXiv:2006.06716v1, printed page 32, are refuted by positive nonconstant solutions of their tree equations of motion. More generally, a positive solution on any connected nontrivial tree of maximum degree at most q+1 extends to T_q by attaching constant-length branches without changing its original vertex ratios. works.abstract_text: The all-length earliest-swapping conjecture in Section IV D 1, Eq. (41), of Kamin, Shchukin, Schmidt and van Loock (2023) states that repeatedly merging an adjacent pair with smallest maximum ready time minimizes total dephasing. We give a self-contained potential proof for arbitrary nonnegative real ready times and every tie choice. The optimum is the largest ready time plus the sum of adjacent maxima minus the sum of ready times. An exact nonnegative slack formula characterizes all optimal histories. The pathwise inequality also answers the exponential-dephasing question in Section IV D 5, for the same fixed-readiness swapping model: earliest swapping simultaneously minimizes expected dephasing and maximizes every expected exponential attenuation factor.

works.abstract_text: We answer Kang–Jäger's Question 1.10 (arXiv:2609.01140v1) negatively, including its strictly ergodic and Toeplitz versions. We construct one aperiodic regular Toeplitz subshift over the binary alphabet such that, for every permutative block code of every length ell >= 2, the entire inverse image is conjugate over the base to the product with the identity on 2^(ell-1) points. Each lift therefore has exactly 2^(ell-1) clopen strictly ergodic components. The construction uses recognizable equal-length words with factorial repetition counts: these annihilate every finite permutation action, while the proportion of columns on which the two words differ is exactly 3^(-n).

For zero-annihilator algebras, the same restriction holds for the semisimple quotient of the derivation algebra, settling the simple-ideal issue in the comment following Conjecture 5. works.abstract_text: Koljančić–Oblak's Problem 1.8, Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra 42 (2026), p. 759, has an affirmative answer: the minimum number of arcs in an n-vertex digraph requiring the nonsymmetric strong spectral property is 2n−1 for every n≥1. By their identification with Arav et al.'s Problem 6.2, this also gives the minimum 2n−1 of nonzero entries in a zero–nonzero pattern requiring the similarity-transversality property (STP). We give a self-contained exposition of the centralizer–incidence proof formalized in Lean. More generally, every real matrix with this property and with c weak support components has at least 2n−c nonzero entries. For connected supports, even allowing one such matrix forces 2n−1 arcs. Together with the endpoint-looped double path of Koljančić–Oblak, this also answers both questions in their Problem 2.9 (p. 764). The endpoint construction is prior work.

works.abstract_text: Question 5.11 of Koljančić and Oblak (arXiv:2604.21552v1, Section 5; journal p. 776) has an affirmative answer: every even double path with a nonempty loop set allows the non-symmetric Strong Spectral Property. We construct a symmetric one-loop witness using coprime branch continuants and prove injectivity of its characteristic-polynomial differential. Openness then supplies every prescribed nonempty loop set. The same argument gives a complete existence criterion in odd order: at least one loop must lie at an odd-numbered vertex. The witnesses can be chosen symmetric with positive integer nonzero entries. Carptopus (19 August 2026) previously proved the full existence criterion and its single-loop spectral characterization. We give an explicit integer construction, an arithmetic criterion for unit edge weights, and the three-way classification for the central-loop and interior-loop families.

works.abstract_text: Extending Maestro's exact qutrit separation (2026) by the unitary-moment obstruction of Dykema and Juschenko (2009), we refute Conjecture 1 of Narasimhachar and Gour (arXiv:1409.7740v3, Supplementary Sec. S2 F, p. S11) even in the closure of finite ground-space thermal transitions. Two diagonal Kraus operators send the uniform pure state of a four-level system with energies 0, 1, 3, 7 to a rank-two state with the same populations. Any energy-conserving realization with an ancilla initially maximally mixed on its full ground eigenspace would express the output correlation matrix as normalized traces of four unitaries. Two linear relations make that representation impossible, with a dimension-independent gap. The trace-norm error of any such thermal output exceeds 10^-8. A three-vector projection obstruction also refutes Conjecture 2 in versions 1 and 2 of the posing source. The four-level obstruction extends to every system with at least four occupied distinct energy levels. Together with the known qutrit closure theorem, this makes four the minimum dimension for closure separation under distinct-level and distinct-gap assumptions.

works.abstract_text: We refute the adjacent-column Conjecture and prove the terminal-column Conjecture in the FORMULA section of Peter Kagey's OEIS entry A378495, revision #70 of October 17, 2026. For n>=5 the corrected adjacent difference is n!/[2(n-2)]=abs(A238474(n-3)); at n=4 it is 3. The literal conjecture fails at n=5, where its sides are 20 and 6. The earliest proof found of the row gcd, both differences and the index correction is Lien-Hung Su, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23445724 v1 (October 18, 2026), Theorem 7.3, Proposition 7.4 and Remark 7.5; Ahaan Kallat gives a later independent proof in arXiv:2610.40342v1 (October 29, 2026), Theorem 4.1. This note gives a self-contained treatment of the differences and their boundary.

works.abstract_text: We prove Mike Sheppard's conjecture in OEIS A381423, Comments, revision 8, that the exponent of the largest signed coefficient of the physicists' Hermite polynomial has successive differences in {1,-3}. A coefficient-ratio calculation gives an explicit formula and proves uniqueness, square-root growth, and the two asserted difference-block lengths. We give exact quadratic indices for the longer blocks. The corresponding absolute-coefficient calculation proves the conjecture in A381524 and the three formulas for equal absolute maxima in A381737. It also gives the absolute mode explicitly, locates its two difference-block types, and determines the asymptotic ratios of successive maximal coefficients.

works.abstract_text: We prove formula (5), COMMENTS (C.1)--(C.10), and the zero clause of COMMENT (C.11) of Paul D. Hanna's OEIS entry A391810, revision 39. For n>=1, the original bilateral Laurent coefficients form a finite row polynomial P_n(y)=-1+sum(h=1..n)y^h(1-y^h)^(n-h). Evaluating it at -1 gives the negative alternating row sum 2 round(2^n/3)=2J_n. The same polynomial proves formulas (2), (3), (4), and (6). Its divisor-sum coefficient expression proves the ten individual-term formulas and T(n,q)=0 for every prime q>n. The further first-zero assertion of (C.11) remains open in this note.

works.abstract_text: We prove the conjecture in Arkadeep Dutta's OEIS A396659, revision 16, FORMULA, third statement: T(n,n^2)/T(n,n^2+1)=(2n-1)/n for every n>=2. Here T(n,k) counts length-k walks from a fixed vertex of the complete looped directed graph on n labeled vertices, visiting every vertex and repeating an edge for the first time at step k. An omitted-edge classification and marked loop insertion prove the ratio. We also establish the entry's two companion formulas, T(n,n+1)=n! and T(n,n^2+1)=(n!)^n, with the linear-walk normalization explicit.

works.abstract_text: We prove Conjectures 9.63 and 9.64 in Section 9.8.3 of Okada's arXiv:2003.02112v2. At unit weights and degree shift zero, every natural width at least three gives a non-almost-palindromic determinant. At width two, almost palindromicity holds exactly when min(a2-a1,b2-b1)=1, giving proportion (lambda-2)(lambda-3)/(lambda(lambda+1)) at b2=lambda>=2. These conclusions hold for every constant positive integral base shift. An infinite family extends the width-two counterexample in Example 9.65. Conjecture 9.66, whose width is at least three, is proved on degree-shift slices e=0,1,G-1,G and at e=G/2 when G is even, where G is the direct-minus-reversed degree gap. The remaining degree shifts are not covered.

works.abstract_text: We refute the conjectures in Section IV immediately after Theorems 1 and 3, Eqs. (10) and (12), of Peled, Te'eni, Carmi and Cohen, Scientific Reports 11, 2849 (2021), that filter normal form can be removed from their correlation-minor bounds. Explicit separable states give robust violations in dimensions 2 by 4 and 2 by D for 5<=D<=8, including positive-definite examples. For every D>=4 and every Schatten parameter, the sharp fourth-order separable bound without filter normal form is 1/(192 sqrt(3)), attained by tetrahedral qubit projectors paired with four orthogonal flags. No common-size pair of regular coherent degree-1 pure designs exists in dimensions 2 and D>=5. We also correct the missing square root in arXiv:2005.12079v2, Appendix D.5, Eq. (D31), using the known separable covariance inequality. The original filter-normal-form theorems retain their scope.

works.abstract_text: We resolve the nonlinear classical k=6 factor-perfection question of Pozsgay and Wanless, §5 immediately after equation (5.13), and their qubit decomposition conjecture in §8 for both constructions studied there (k=6,8). For arbitrary finite-alphabet gates, a perfect six-leg composite forces perfect factors. Six specified permutation flattenings characterize this property. A norm–determinant argument gives the quantum analogue for unitary gates, extending the prior forward construction of §3.2, Theorems 1–2. For arbitrary complex factors, the same six unitary exterior flattenings guarantee perfect replacement tensors at the same bond dimension. This excludes every six-qubit AME state from the three-vertex triangle with bond dimension two. The eight-qubit case follows from known AME nonexistence (Rains, DOI 10.1109/18.796376; Scott, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevA.69.052330).

works.abstract_text: We prove the affirmative answer to MathOverflow question 516405, revision 1: the second ordinary adjacency eigenvalue of deterministic inner-face Apollonian networks divided by 2^(m/2) tends to sqrt(2). For every fixed rank r, the largest and smallest adjacency eigenvalues divided by 2^(m/2) converge to plus and minus sqrt(d_r), where the decreasing weight sequence consists of 3, three copies of 2, and 3^j copies of 3*2^(-j) for each j >= 1. An exact cutoff Gram identity gives a finite-stage bound and an O_r(2^(-m/4)) rate. The original second-eigenvalue limit is the scope of the pinned Lean declaration; the fixed-rank and quantitative extensions have written proofs.

works.abstract_text: We resolve Question III.5 of Stepanov, Herrmann and Guhr (arXiv:2104.08966v1, p. 7): on the remaining domain D = A minus (A1 union A2), correlation matrices with prescribed mean c and standard deviation sigma and a nonmaximal top-eigenvector weight in every orthonormal eigenbasis exist in every sufficiently large dimension exactly when sigma > c. Centered spectral moments exclude the diagonal, and a positive definite rank-two construction gives existence above it. Throughout the legal half-disc sigma >= 0, c^2 + sigma^2 <= 1, eventual existence holds exactly for 0 <= c < 1/2, sigma > c and c^2 + sigma^2 < 1. A spectral-projection criterion treats eigenvalue multiplicities and shows that a rank-one boundary matrix has the universal gap exactly when c < 0.

works.abstract_text: The Shannon conjecture following Eq. (69) in Section V.C of Tarabunga et al., arXiv:2411.05766v1, is false. An explicit three-qubit state has stabilizer-basis entropy log 4, whereas the proposed absolute-amplitude lower bound is log 16 - (9/8) log 3 > log 4. The same construction refutes the bound for nonnegative amplitudes, and continuity gives strictly positive examples. It extends to every N >= 3 and to a range of Renyi indices containing one. The collision entropy of the comparison distribution remains a valid Shannon lower bound for arbitrary affine supports. For amplitudes of constant modulus on each affine coset, the original bound holds at every Renyi index; this includes the source's Figure 1 product states.

works.abstract_text: We resolve User3's question (question 515549, revision 1, September 25, 2026): for every nonsingular real square matrix of positive size, the orthogonal minimum of rho(|PQ||Q^T P^{-1}|) is attained and equals one. Thus the proposed strict uniform lower bound cannot hold for any such matrix. We give a self-contained exposition of the triangularization proof in the pinned formal source, then characterize every minimizer by independent row and column permutations to triangular form. For fixed P, the set of minimizers is finite and has an explicit description using row-permuted QR factorizations. The same minimum holds over the special orthogonal group. Finally, the companion absolute-row-sum balancing question follows from the Yamabe-Yujobo theorem.

works.abstract_text: We refute Conjectures 3.26 and 5.3 of Wang's Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups (arXiv:2509.18724v1, pp. 23 and 27). The commutative periodic monoid of finite subsets of the natural numbers, paired with levels zero, one and two under union and capped addition, has algebraic Davenport constant one over every nonzero commutative unitary ring. Its nongroup relative Davenport constants are unbounded. The finite submonoids with supports contained in {1,...,m}, m>=1, have the same algebraic constant, whereas the expression conjectured to equal it grows without bound as m increases.

works.abstract_text: For OEIS A344611, FORMULA (revision 27), we prove A344611(n) <= A160786(n) for every n >= 0 and give an alternative derivation of Manyama's (2026) convolution, complementing Andrews–El Bachraoui's (2026) strict-partition formulas. An injection sends a partition with nonnegative reverse-alternating sum to an odd-length partition of the next weight. We characterize equality, give an explicit lower bound for the deficit, and deduce monotonicity of the corresponding unrestricted count. The same parity analysis proves a shifted companion comparison, determines all plateaus of the negative-sum count, and corrects neighboring indexing and distinct-part descriptions. A bivariate series settles the linked ordered-composition interpretations, with their precise shifts.

works.abstract_text: The question in Xu et al., Section 4.2, page 12 of arXiv:2211.05563v1, asks whether the optimized witness bound equals the convex-roof geometric measure of genuine multipartite entanglement for noisy GHZ states. A strict separation holds for every party count n >= 3 and local dimension d >= 3 at an explicit noise probability. For three qutrits at noise p=3/8, the optimized witness bound is exactly 1/9, whereas the convex roof is at least 13/108. A biseparable overlap inequality and a positive-definite matrix give a two-observable lower bound. A written corollary extends the three-qutrit strict gap throughout 27/74 < p < 9/22.
